sections.title: Links that jump to a terminal

items.title: A `ghoztty://` link can raise a window or pane
items.text: Write `ghoztty://focus/<name>` anywhere a link can live and clicking it brings that Ghoztty window or pane to the front. `<name>` is anything `--target` already accepts: a window name, an auto `window-3`, a pane name, or a pane id (`$GHOZTTY_PANE_ID`). A generated dashboard, a build report, or a status page can finally say "jump to that terminal" and have it work.

items.title: It works everywhere a link renders
items.text: From your browser, from a page or rendered markdown in a viewer pane, and from a pane banner. Banner focus links get their own right-click menu (Focus in Ghoztty / Copy Link) instead of the side-pane and new-window options, which don't mean anything for a link that names a window rather than content.

items.title: Focus is the only thing a link can do, on purpose
items.text: Any web page you visit can fire a registered URL scheme with no prompt and no way to tell who asked. A link that could open a shell or type into a pane would be remote code execution behind an `<a href>`, so raising an existing window is the whole feature. Nothing is ever created: a link naming a window that's gone tells you so instead of quietly focusing something else, and a burst of links produces one message rather than one per link.

items.title: Debug builds keep their links to themselves
items.text: The debug build registers `ghoztty-debug://`, so macOS can't decide to route your links into a development build. Links clicked inside Ghoztty are handled in-process, so a document that hardcodes `ghoztty://` still lands in whichever build is rendering it.
